decision_lens: Prioritize whether the proposed debate has the formal-rebuttal structure (objection → reply → counter) that makes disputatio rigorous, or is just unstructured back-and-forth that happens to span two rounds. Critique whether the lead's determinatio (synthesis) is constrained by what survived rebuttal or is free to confabulate.
distance_rationale: A medieval/Renaissance university genre of formal debate with codified move types and an authoritative determinatio bound to the dispute — predates and is alien to modern AI-orchestration vocabulary while sharing the multi-party-bounded-discourse-with-final-synthesis shape.
expected_isomorphisms: The objection-reply-determinatio sequence transfers as a per-round move-grammar that distinguishes 'argument turn', 'rebuttal turn', and 'binding-synthesis turn'. The determinatio-bound-by-dispute principle transfers as a synthesis acceptance criterion that synthesis only assert what survived challenge.
focus: Scholastic disputatio as a formal debate genre with respondens, opponentes, and praeses roles, structured objections-and-replies, and a master's determinatio that is bound by what was actually disputed
name: fd-renaissance-disputatio
persona: Apply the perspective of a historian of the medieval/Renaissance scholastic disputatio — a formal academic exercise where a respondens defended a thesis, opponentes raised structured objections, a praeses moderated form, and after a fixed number of objection-rounds the master delivered a determinatio that had to address every objection that survived reply, with the genre's discipline coming from the requirement that every move be answerable in kind.
review_areas: Whether round 1's 'state strongest candidates and challenge one peer' is symmetrically obligatory (every debater both states and challenges) or asymmetric in a way that produces uneven move-counts
Whether round 2's 'respond to challenges' is a required reply-to-each-objection (sed contra) or a soft acknowledgement that lets challenges go unaddressed
Whether the lead's synthesis is constrained to only assert isomorphisms that survived a challenge unanswered or successfully answered, rather than free-form summary
Whether the move grammar is encoded in the prompts (you must address objection X in form Y) or left to chance
Whether the spec JSONs feeding debater prompts function as auctoritates (cited authorities) the debaters must engage with, or just as backstory

Whether the TaskCompleted hook understands the difference between 'rounds done, all objections answered' and 'rounds done, some objections orphaned' — and whether orphaned objections appear in the synthesis as unresolved tensions

severity_examples.condition: Debater prompt for round 2 reads 'respond OR propose new combinations' rather than 'respond to each challenge first, then propose'
severity_examples.scenario: Round 2 prompt allows debaters to introduce new arguments instead of replying to round-1 objections, losing the objection-reply discipline

severity_examples.condition: Synthesis acceptance criteria do not require an 'unresolved tensions' section
severity_examples.scenario: The synthesis is not constrained to acknowledge unresolved objections, so the lead can write a clean doc that papers over genuine disagreement

severity_examples.condition: Round 1 prompt does not require each debater to issue at least one challenge
severity_examples.scenario: Symmetric-challenge requirement (each debater challenges one peer) is unstated, so a debater could opt to challenge no one and break the mesh

task_context: Reviewing a 2-round debate brainstorm where rounds are described loosely. Looking for whether move grammar is rigorous enough to make the debate produce determinatio-grade synthesis rather than vibe-summary.
